title: Dynamic curve · Simple or layered curves
slide_intent: Teach designers to compare two levels of visual detail while holding the underlying shape steady. A matched pair lets a reader see exactly what the added layers contribute.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can give flat and tonal treatments a shared profile. The same off-center placement recurs in both finished examples.
demonstration: Two columns pair a construction diagram with a finished red sample. One uses a single arc and flat fill. The other retains the circular center arc and adds two edges with tonal differences.
practical_value: Choose a single flat boundary or a layered treatment by comparing the two finished samples at equal size. Preserve the common circular arc when adding the extra edges.

content_islands.name: Variant definitions
content_islands.spec: Set the shared device name and comparison title above the page. Place one compact definition per variant in the left column.

content_islands.name: Construction pair
content_islands.spec: Align two equal frames across the top. Mark the shared X and 2X divisions. Show one edge in the left frame and three numbered tonal areas with the center arc identified in the right.

content_islands.name: Finished pair
content_islands.spec: Below the corresponding diagrams, place two red-and-white samples at the same size. Keep the left fill flat and show the light band and darker tonal transition in the right.
